title: Genetics and Inheritance
seo_title: SSS 3 Biology: Genetics and Inheritance Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_text: Genes, alleles, genotype and phenotype; monohybrid crosses with complete dominance, incomplete dominance and co-dominance; sex determination; sex-linked inheritance (haemophilia, colour blindness); blood groups; dihybrid crosses; pedigree diagrams; mutations; genetic engineering, cloning and paternity testing. (summary of the senior secondary Biology curriculum, SSS 3; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 Biology worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): monohybrid crosses, dihybrid crosses and linkage, sex linkage and pedigrees, dihybrid crosses and other patterns and sex-linked traits and disorders. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A dominant allele shows in the phenotype if present.
key_sub: Tt × Tt gives a 3 : 1 phenotype ratio.
body_html:
How to think about it

A gene has different forms called alleles. The genotype is the pair of alleles (TT, Tt, tt); the phenotype is the characteristic that shows. In complete dominance Tt looks like TT. In incomplete dominance the heterozygote is intermediate (red × white → pink); in co-dominance both alleles show (blood group AB).

Sex is determined by the X and Y chromosomes: XX female, XY male. Sex-linked alleles such as haemophilia are carried on the X chromosome, so they are more common in males. A dihybrid cross of two heterozygotes (TtRr × TtRr) gives a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 phenotype ratio.

Example

Tt × tt. Proportion of tall offspring?

Punnett square

Answer: 50%

Example

A man with haemophilia (XʰY) has a son with a normal woman (XᴴXᴴ). Chance the son has haemophilia?

Sons get the father's Y.

Answer: 0%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dominant means more common.
  • Thinking a son can inherit an X-linked allele from his father.
  • Mixing up genotype and phenotype.

faq.q: Why are more males colour-blind than females?
faq.a: Males have only one X chromosome, so one recessive allele is enough.

faq.q: How can blood groups show that a man is not a child's father?
faq.a: If the child has an allele that neither the mother nor the man could have passed on.

items.q: In snapdragons, the cross Cᴿ Cᵂ × Cᴿ Cᴿ (codominant) is made. What proportion of the offspring are red (Cᴿ Cᴿ)?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Cᴿ Cᵂ × Cᴿ Cᴿ (codominant) and count the matching boxes: 12.

items.q: In pea, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt × Tt) give 108 offspring. How many are expected to be tall?
items.e: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so ¾ of 108 = 81.
